bounds.domain: Seven PR admission lanes, four mandatory Quint partitions on main PR/merge-queue contexts, and one production main Full admission with two logical validation epochs (including a rerun of an older run ID) and three independent predicates (exact GitHub identity, complete current-source rows, staging certification). Other PR branches require Quint skipped. Actual canonical CI also requires the four-shard aggregate on main push/manual/reusable contexts regardless of changed paths.
bounds.assumptions: GitHub supplies trustworthy run/artifact metadata for the requested repository and protects workflow source at its exact SHA. The hook executes real YAML result shell gates, all event/branch classifiers, source-bound shard validation, actual Git manifest/ZIP consumers and existing ledger/staging tests with controlled API fixtures. Production gates run at migration/image/Worker/Pages mutation boundaries. Admission linearizes at final metadata recheck; a future rerun after admission does not retroactively revoke an already-started effect. Completed reruns are bound to their per-attempt metadata; any active exact-source run or ambiguous start ordering blocks admission. Staging is verified before the final main snapshot, and returned expiry is the earlier proof expiry, checked again immediately before mutation.
bounds.limitations: Finite boolean identity/row/staging projection and at most one concurrent rerun; file bytes/hashes, arbitrary API histories, network failure timing and provider effects are outside the model. Tests exercise real Git/ZIP/current manifest code with synthetic GitHub responses; no actual GitHub dispatch/deployment, branch protection deployment, physical device or service availability claim. Current expected manifest is recomputed from the trusted exact-source checkout. Fair completion assumes reads/decisions return; unavailable GitHub remains fail closed.

assumptions: Weak fairness settles every running mandatory lane and evaluates the enabled aggregate. No particular successful outcome is assumed.
No fairness or service availability is assumed. A permanently running lane can prevent the aggregate from completing.
Every running shard settles and the enabled evidence check and aggregate evaluation are weakly fair. Valid evidence is not assumed.
Read and decision scheduling are weakly fair and finite API work returns; successful evidence is not assumed.
